doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Meeting Frank Sinatra at the Harry James band, Hotel Sherman
summary: Ware and his group sit in after the Harry James band at the Hotel Sherman, and Sinatra buys him a sausage and says he is going with Tommy Dorsey.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Well, I was working down there with Buster Bennett like I said, at the old Tuxedo Inn, and it kind of closed, and I went back out hustling again with the fellows. And we wound up one night -- we went up to Harry James -- across the street from the Hotel Sherman, the Panther Room, and he was sitting in a little bar, and he come over and said, 'Come on in -- maybe you could join the tail end of the show and see what you can do.' And they had -- I'll never forget this --

Meade Lux Albert Ammons they had Meade Lux Lewis, Alan Edwards, Joe Turner, Pete Johnson, and the Harry James band, and Frank Sinatra was singing with them. And I don't know -- I hope I don't get in no trouble for saying it, but I met him, and we come back stage and the guys were saying just stand here, they were playing; they had just broadcasted -- they were broadcasting nightly -- and Sinatra was just talking to them; he said, "I'm Frank Sinatra" and he says "You hungry?" and I said, "Yeah" and he went back and bought me a sausage.

And after he came back from singing he says, "I'm gonna be a big star one of these days. This is my last week, and I'm going with Tommy Dorsey." And I was amazed that he'd even talk to me, you know. Like I said, I was just a kid, and being on the South Side, you didn't fraternize too much with the white people, you know.

I'll never forget it, though, he gave me a picture -- I lost that picture back in 1955; somebody stole my belongings, because I had messed up; if they didn't steal them then I left them there, never did find them misplaced them. But I moved out of this room, -- but I remember that; we went out that night, and oh my God, we played, we sang "The Lamp is Low" -- I'll never forget the routine we did. "The Lamp is Low" -- we did "The Sheik of Arabee" and we closed with "Tiger Rag" which we used as a flash, and we brought the house to their feet.
